plan: Economists suggest bidding your value as a dominant strategy, meaning it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. My value is $15, so I will bid $15. This ensures that if I win, my profit equals my value minus the second-highest bid, optimizing my earnings. Since this is the only round, I have no history to consider, reinforcing the strategy of bidding my value.

Economists suggest bidding your exact value is optimal. Since my value is $36, bidding this maximizes expected profit. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, gaining the difference between my value and that bid. Since this is the only round, there's no need to consider long-term strategies or adapt from previous rounds. Thus, I will bid exactly $36 to maximize my chance of winning without overpaying.

The dominant strategy in this auction game is to bid your private value, which maximizes expected profit. My private value is $42. By bidding my value, I ensure that I only win if the second-highest bid is less than or equal to $42, thus maximizing my potential profit. Since there is no history to consider from previous rounds, I will rely on this strategy for optimal results.
